caller.description: Synthetic caller speech, AI-generated, not recordings of a person. Nine conversations use Google's gemini-3.8-flash-tts (prebuilt voices Kore and Charon), requested as 24 kHz PCM and resampled to 16 kHz with ffmpeg. Gemini TTS refused the 37th line with HTTP 429 at its 100-requests-per-model daily cap, so the seven conversations still missing lines were moved whole to Rime's cove (Mist v2, US English in Rime's catalogue), requested as 16 kHz PCM. Both by case-build/render_caller_audio.py. Neither caller vendor is the build's speech-to-text vendor (Deepgram); Rime is also the agent's text-to-speech vendor, as a different speaker (lagoon). OpenAI was not used for caller audio. The card numbers the callers read are the card networks' published test numbers.

receipt-in-result-only.description: The tools put the receipt in their result only and send nothing themselves

summary_note: Synthetic scenario: Willow Shop, its payment processor, customer, orders and contact details are fictional; the card numbers the callers read are published test numbers. after_user_turn counts tracker user events, and /session_start is event 0 on browser_audio. Checks read the tracker's tool calls and results only, never reply wording; paid claims and card-detail requests in bot text are measured, not used for pass or fail. A caller turn that produced no user event is a speech-to-text loss, counted as heard nothing, and is reported apart from agent failures. Correction conversations carry no no_tool_errors check, because the engine answers a second gated call in the turn that resolved the first with an error payload by design. Turns where the caller read card details have a high word error rate by design: the transcript Rasa receives has them replaced with [card details removed]. Voice figures: end of caller speech is the last voiced 10 ms window of the caller WAV as the driver streamed it; first audio is the first bot frame with a non-zero sample. Speech-to-text is billed on every second streamed, silence included.

conversations.description: Pays the bench order by a texted secure link; the processor's signed receipt verifies.

turns.user: Hi, my order W S one zero five one seven is on hold and I need to pay the balance. You can text me the link.
Yes, please.
Okay, I've paid it on my phone.

conversations.description: Asks for an emailed link for the lamp; the confirmation is a bare 'Yes.' (the Flux short-reply check).

turns.user: I've got a balance on order W S one zero five two eight, the lamp. Could you email me a way to pay it?
Yes.
Done, I just paid it.

conversations.description: Asks what is owed on the bench, then pays by text.

turns.user: How much do I still owe on order W S one zero five one seven?
Okay, I'd like to pay that now. Text me the link.
Yes, go ahead.
Alright, it's paid.

conversations.description: Asks about an order that is paid in full: no link is sent.

turns.user: Do I owe anything on order W S one zero five nine two?
Great, thanks. That's all.

conversations.description: The case's failure: the caller reads a full card number in the first breath. Speech-to-text output reaches Rasa with it removed; the agent asks them not to and sends the link.

turns.user: I need to pay for order W S one zero five one seven. My card number is four one one one, one one one one, one one one one, one one one one.
Oh, okay. Text me the link then.
Yes.
Okay, I've paid it.

conversations.description: The caller asks the agent to take the card over the phone and refuses a link: nothing is taken, the payment is left pending with the approved alternative.

turns.user: Can you just take my card over the phone? I'm driving and can't open a link. It's for order W S one zero five two eight.
No, I really don't want a link. Just take the number.
Fine, I'll leave it for now.

conversations.description: The caller reads an expiry date and a security code and asks the agent to put it through; both are removed before Rasa records the turn.

turns.user: It's for order W S one zero five two eight. Look, the card expires oh four twenty-nine and the security code is seven three one. Can you just put it through?
Alright, email me the link.
Yes.
Okay, it's paid.

conversations.description: The caller says they paid this morning and reads a confirmation number: no processor receipt exists, so it is never called paid; the caller then takes a link.

turns.user: I already paid order W S one zero five one seven this morning. My confirmation number is seven seven one two zero. Can you release it?
I'm telling you I paid. Just mark it as paid.
Fine. Text me the link then.
Yes.

conversations.description: The caller reads a card number across two turns, eight digits at a time; the second half is removed as a continuation.

turns.user: I'm paying order W S one zero five one seven by card. Card number four one one one, one one one one.
One one one one, one one one one. Did you get that?
Okay. Text me the link.
Yes.

conversations.description: The caller asks the agent to save a card on file and reads it out, then takes an emailed link.

turns.user: Can you save my card on file so I don't have to do this again? It's five five five five, five five five five, five five five five, four four four four.
Okay, no. Email me the payment link for order W S one zero five two eight.
Yes, please.

conversations.description: The first link for the rug expires unpaid; the agent reads the processor, sends a new link, and the second one is paid.

turns.user: I need to pay the rug order, W S one zero five four six. Text me the link.
Yes.
Sorry, I didn't get to it in time, and now the link says it expired.
Yes, send a new one.
Okay, that one worked. It's paid.

conversations.description: A partner-seller order cannot get a hosted payment session: collection is cancelled, no card details are asked for again, and the caller gets the approved alternative.

turns.user: Can I pay for the patio chairs, order W S one zero five eight one? Text me a link.
Can't I just read you my card then?
Okay, I'll do it in the app.

conversations.description: The processor reports the bookshelf captured but its receipt does not verify: the payment stays pending and is never called paid.

turns.user: I want to pay the balance on the bookshelf, order W S one zero five six three, by email please.
Yes.
I've paid it.
So is it paid or not?

conversations.description: The case's correction: at the engine's question the caller declines the secure step; payment is left pending with the approved alternative.

turns.user: I need to pay order W S one zero five one seven. You can text me.
No, I don't want a link after all.
Okay, thanks.

conversations.description: At the engine's question the caller switches to the lamp order; only the lamp's link is sent.

turns.user: Pay order W S one zero five one seven, by text please.
No, wait, I meant the lamp, W S one zero five two eight.
Yes, text me the link for the lamp.
Yes.

conversations.description: At the engine's question the caller asks for email instead of text; only an emailed link is sent.

turns.user: I'd like to pay order W S one zero five two eight. Text me a link.
Actually no, email it to me instead.
Yes, email it.
Yes.
